A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTO study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-representation analyses, classifier experiments, reasoning benchmark results, sensitivity studies, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds decoded-token case studies, additional model and benchmark evaluations, and Llama-3-8B resource measurements.

M1.justification: The LRM architecture, pooling, classification loss, KL-regularized objective, and sampling procedure in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of normalization and general-LLM hidden states do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The original five datasets are retained. v3 adds MATH and graduate-level GPQA evaluations in Appendix H.6, substantially broadening reasoning difficulty and task coverage, plus a one-digit arithmetic task for interpretability analysis in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in retained experiments, including the answer-correction methods, CoE-R, CoE-C, and weighted majority voting. Added general-LLM evaluations retain the base-model and majority-voting comparisons. Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B are additional evaluated backbones.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B configurations and a diagnostic protocol decoding the top five tokens at steps 16, 32, 48, and 64. Appendix C.4 changes the reported intrinsic-dimension trimming fraction from 0.9 to 0.1; this establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that the existing plots were recomputed.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds six arithmetic case studies examining whether correct answer tokens emerge and stabilize during latent thinking. Appendix H.7 extends efficiency analysis to Llama-3-8B. Existing aggregation, sampling-budget, beta, thinking-step, and cross-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 revises the outlier-trimming fraction used by the Two-Nearest-Neighbour intrinsic-dimension estimator from 0.9 to 0.1, changing a reported statistical-estimation setting. Otherwise, significance reporting retains the p < 0.05 convention, with no added repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for new settings in Tables A4–A5 and Llama-3-8B resource measurements in Tables A8–A9. For example, Table A5 reports Llama-3-8B MATH correctness of 0.375 for LTO versus 0.335 for majority voting, and Qwen-3-4B GPQA correctness of 0.490 versus 0.368. Original Tables 1–2 and A1–A3 retain their numerical results; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, assumptions, and final bounds are retained, but their derivations receive corrections. v3 Appendix F.2 fixes summation indices in the acceptance-probability calculation, and F.3 replaces erroneous reward-normalization terms with perfect-reward terms in the KL derivation, correcting expressions in v1 Appendices E.2–E.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: latent thoughts predict correctness, LRMs enable probabilistic thinking optimization, and the approach extends across domains and general LLMs. Added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds an explanation of how KL regularization limits exploitation of reward-model errors and policy collapse. Appendix D interprets decoded-token trajectories, while Section 6.3 explicitly acknowledges that full transferability across all tasks has not been demonstrated. The existing limitations concerning incorrect candidate sets and correctness-only rewards remain.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies existing RMSNorm normalization and layer-to-step construction for general-LLM LRMs, adds Llama-3-8B timing and memory information, and replaces the anonymous code/data link with a named repository link. However, Appendix G.2 omits the explicit default beta = 1e-3 stated in v1 Appendix F.2.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting MATH, GPQA, Llama 3, and Qwen3 experiments. Appendix A's research positioning remains essentially unchanged. Updated authorship and publication information for existing references, including GPT-4, Gemini, and the reasoning-model survey, do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: v3 corrects the recurring Huggin/Huginn spelling and other language errors, expands several explanations, and adds appendix subsections and an LLM-usage statement. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands displayed evidence with decoded-token Figure A2 and Tables A4, A5, A8, and A9; Table A4 partly redisplays existing Llama-2 results. Original efficiency tables remain as A6–A7. Classifier plots are regrouped by dataset, and Figure 3's reversed SVAMP/MBPP captions are corrected.

improvement.justification: The added harder-benchmark evaluations, newer backbones, decoded-token examples, and general-LLM cost measurements strengthen empirical support and interpretability. Corrected Figure 3 labels and proof expressions improve accuracy. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new benchmark protocols and removal of the explicit default beta, producing a modest net improvement.
